### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via retryConfig (literal, a string literal in undeclaredNestedKeysOf))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via publishedDefinition (literal, a string literal in redactServedDocument))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retryConfig (literal, a string literal in undeclaredNestedKeysOf))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e21776503575b90ceec8546459f27b442930383a` — the merge of head `8daa64f14fc48cfb00e99cc3a400b6c609172db3` into base `ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e21776503575b90ceec8546459f27b442930383a && git checkout e21776503575b90ceec8546459f27b442930383a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f 8daa64f14fc48cfb00e99cc3a400b6c609172db3 && git checkout -B drift-repro ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f && git merge --no-ff 8daa64f14fc48cfb00e99cc3a400b6c609172db3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8daa64f14fc48cfb00e99cc3a400b6c609172db3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.ts + packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts (`RetryConfigSchema`, `ConnectorActionSchema`, the entry's `retryConfig` and `actions` bindings), packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-credential-fields.ts (`objectShapeOf`, `wrapperChainOf`, `walkDeclaredFields`), packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts (the registry), packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-redaction.ts (`identityOf`, `elementWithIdentity`, `resolveHops`, `locate`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (the served reads, the per-package list the package export reads), packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts (`getPublished`, `redactServedBody`, `redactServedDocument`, `publishPackage`), packages/metadata/src/stored-envelope.ts (`STORED_ENVELOPE_KEYS`), packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-credential-projection.ts (the one other redactor that names array paths), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (the publish door), packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts (the published read)

Round 2 on this head. Round 1 was a FAIL on `1fed7aac` (one must-fix in the published read's bookkeeping pass-through, now fixed and pinned; one should-fix in the redactor's handling of a malformed nested container, now closed). This record stands on its own: it covers the whole PR, two commits on `main` at `3ac22c9d` (the merged #28764), with no force push.

Inputs read: the PR body, both commits and their messages, the changeset, the eight changed files at the head, the net diff against the merge-base and the interdiff from `1fed7aac`, the cited code at the head, the two #28764 review records (comments 6562139912 and 6563090347), the claim on #28284 (comment 6568020317), the open PRs touching the same files, and the check-runs on the head. No card exists by design.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **What the connector read now withholds, nested.** Inside `retryConfig` and inside each element of `actions`, every key `RetryConfigSchema` and `ConnectorActionSchema` do not declare is withheld whole, whatever its value, cleared forms included. The declared sets are read from the two schemas' own shapes through `objectShapeOf`, which walks the lazy wrapper to the object; an unreadable shape leaves the set empty and withholds every nested key, failing closed. The entry binds the same two schemas, so no declared nested key is withheld. Right.
2. **A nested container that is not the declared shape.** A `retryConfig` that is not an object, and an `actions` that is not an array or holds an element that is not an object, are withheld whole and named as `retryConfig` or `actions`; a cleared form (`null`, `''`, `{}`) and an empty list are served as written. This is the posture the module already takes for a non-object `auth`, and an element is never removed alone, so no index shifts. The spec pins cover four malformed shapes and the cleared-form control; the protocol pin shows the served form saves and keeps the stored value at rest. Right.
3. **On which exits.** The withholding sits inside the one registry entry every body-serving exit resolves: the item read, the list in both spellings, the layered read, the history diff, the generic row door, the published read, and the per-package list the package export reads. The execution reads apply no serving decoration, by design. Right.
4. **The paths named.** `retryConfig.KEY` and `actions.INDEX.KEY` (the element by its index), or the container's own name when it is withheld whole; sorted with the rest of `redactedKeys`. `withoutKeyAt` copies an array hop and `readAt` reads through one. The input is never mutated and is returned by reference when nothing is withheld. Right.
5. **`MetadataManager.getPublished` and `redactServedBody`.** The served body is walked by `redactServedDocument`: a key outside `STORED_ENVELOPE_KEYS` is the authored document and goes to the type's redactor; a scalar bookkeeping value (`packageId`, `package`, `state`, `version`, `publishedAt`, `publishedBy`, all strings or numbers as `publishPackage` writes them) is served beside the answer unchanged; a `publishedDefinition` that is an object is a document of the same type and goes through the same redaction at every depth; any other non-scalar bookkeeping value is not served. The input is returned by reference only when nothing at any depth changed. For every type with a redactor, the published read now serves no document that the type's redactor has not judged. Pinned in the metadata unit test (two legs, the first guarding its own guard) and in a dogfood `/published` leg for a member and for an administrator. Right; the round-1 must-fix is closed.
6. **Carry-forward identity by `key`.** `identityOf` returns `id` when present, otherwise a non-empty string `key`. Read in every path producer: the flow redactor addresses nodes, which carry `id`, and regions, which carry neither and are anchored as before; the datasource and derived redactors name no array path. In the tree today only a connector action is followed by `key`, as the changeset says; the twin-key case carries neither, the existing rule, and is pinned. Right.
7. **Declared keys, execution reads and the served-form save.** The save door's order is unchanged; a served form carries only declared nested keys, so the nested shapes accept it; each nested entry in `redactedKeys` resolves at the standard split, the `actions` hop by the element's `key`, and the position check keeps the graft because the redactor still withholds it. A removed `retryConfig` or element is not minted back. The control pins a `credentialRef` instance that saves, reaches ready and dispatches. Right.
8. **Public surface.** No package entry reaches `redactConnectorItem`, `identityOf` or `redactServedDocument`; `redactServedBody` is private. No published export changes. Right.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset at the head: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`, `'@objectstack/metadata': patch`; `Clause-②: no`; `Metadata-protocol: none`. The PR body carries the same two lines, and every package the diff moves is named.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: the two nested shapes still accept what they accepted, every save that succeeded before succeeds now, and no key, value or type is added, removed or re-meant.
- `Clause-②: no` holds, on the reading the #28764 records set for this function: the read serves fewer keys of a stored row, but every withheld position is outside the declared sets, no declared capability leaves the consumer, and the carry-forward change only carries more. The `(narrowing)` arm would be owed only if the nested write shapes were closed, which this PR does not do.
- The level follows the kind alone: `none` takes `patch` on every entry, and no authorable-surface baseline moves. Consistent with `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and ruling A on #25105; Check Changeset is green on the head.
- Disclosure: the changeset, both commit messages and the source comments (module note item 8, the `redactServedBody` docblock) say what is hardened and how behaviour changes, in product words; the maintainer's "为什么改" line is present verbatim in the 维护者速读 and under `## Why`. No breach.

### ③ Boundary flags

The PR's `user.login` is `os-project-manager`, not `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: the seat's own account. Named here; the seat reads this before landing.

1. **Open question: narrowing the nested write shapes.** Answer: not needed for this PR's hardening, and not owed by it. The write side is a separate `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` card, with a census of what the ADR-0023 and ADR-0024 generators and the hand-registered path put on an action first. The seat decides whether to open it; it does not block this PR.
2. **Out-of-scope findings in the hand-back.** Both stand as separate cards; neither is a gap this PR should close.
3. **PR body is the round-1 text. should-fix, prose, before ACCEPT.** The "What changes" bullet still says a non-object `retryConfig` or element is not walked, and the `getPublished` bullet still says the bookkeeping is served unchanged; both describe `1fed7aac`. The Verification section is stamped on `1fed7aac`, the test counts predate the second commit (the spec file now holds more cases than the 两分钟验证 line expects), and the ablation table lacks the second commit's leg. Prose is the lane seat's face; the ACCEPT reads the body against this head.
4. **Overlap.** Open PR #28920 touches `connector.zod.ts` (an `oauth2` instance key) and one line of the redaction test's declared-not-a-secret list; no hunk coincides with this PR's, so the later of the two to land rebases cleanly.
5. **Check-runs on the head at record time.** 13 success, 12 skipped, 0 red, 13 still in progress (Build Core, Build UI Deps, Plan Test Core shards and the Test Core shards behind it, Live E2E UI, the Type Check and Lint families). Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint · PM dispatch-gates and the PR-body guards are green. No red is known. The landing rule wants every check green, so the seat re-reads the head before queueing.

### ④ Design judgment

- `undeclaredNestedKeysOf` is a sibling of `undeclaredRootKeysOf`, run first with the same no-cleared-form rule for keys and the module's existing whole-container rule for a malformed shape; item 8 of the module note now records both next to item 7, in product words.
- `redactServedDocument` is one walk for the document and the bookkeeping, with the one document-valued bookkeeping key handled by recursion and every other non-scalar value failing closed. The reference-return rule is kept, so a clean body still serves by identity.
- The `key` fallback sits in `identityOf` alone, so the ambiguity guard, the anchor rule and the relocation by identity apply unchanged.

Findings: no must-fix. One should-fix, ③ 3 (prose, the lane seat's face). Two notes, ③ 1 and ③ 2.
